# Benchmark results

Target: x86_64-windows. Each cell is the median of 7 runs in a fresh process.

## Time per operation

Nanoseconds per operation (lower is better), with millions of operations per second in parentheses. An operation is one allocator call, except in `vec-growth` and `hashmap`, where it is one push or one insert or removal, most of which do not allocate. Lab allocators run with the `stats` feature on.

## Memory at the peak

Internal: share of the memory taken from the allocator that no request asked for (headers, rounding, padding). External: share of the free memory that is not in the largest free block. The system allocator does not expose either.

## Scenarios

- `small-fixed`: 20 000 blocks of 32 bytes, then free in order.
- `random`: 50 000 random alloc/free steps, 8 to 2048 bytes.
- `fifo`: 10 000 random-size blocks, freed in allocation order.
- `lifo`: 10 000 random-size blocks, freed in reverse order.
- `stack`: 50 000 random push/pop steps on a stack of blocks.
- `fragment`: free every other block, then ask for larger ones.
- `vec-growth`: 20 Vec<u64> grown to 100 000 elements by push.
- `hashmap`: HashMap<u64, u64>: 50 000 inserts, removals, reinserts.
- `game-frame`: 200 frames of 1 000 short-lived allocations each.
